payload.impact: pricing-api only: repeated container-scoped cgroup OOM terminations (Last State OOMKilled, exit code 137) as memory working set approaches the 256Mi limit. The injected mismatch is JVM -Xmx512m versus a 256Mi container limit, but causality requires corroborating cgroup, JVM, and telemetry evidence.

supports: The affected pod runs on vm-4, so node-level exhaustion is a possible general cause of exit 137.

payload.rationale: The JVM accepted an approximately 512Mi maximum heap while the container is limited to 256Mi; Kubernetes recorded OOMKilled/137 restarts while the node had no memory pressure. Restore the likely known-safe 128Mi heap ceiling, retaining the existing 256Mi limit and 128Mi of cgroup headroom for metaspace, code cache, native memory, and JVM/process overhead. This is a single reversible Deployment-template change and does not affect persistent data.
payload.rollback_trigger: Execute the rollback if the replacement pod cannot become or remain Ready, exhibits a new OOMKilled termination or restart, or fails either SLO threshold in any of the 3 required post-recovery windows.

success_criteria.description: The replacement pod becomes Ready and remains available with no additional container restarts or OOMKilled terminations while benchmark load runs; for each of 3 consecutive post-recovery SLO windows, HTTP 5xx rate is below 0.001 and p95 latency is below 200 ms.

critical_claims.claim: The pricing-api JVM was configured with -Xmx512m while its container memory limit was 256Mi; runtime logging confirmed maxHeap=518979584.
The container was terminated as OOMKilled with exit code 137 after a three-second run and had restarted twice.
Node-wide memory pressure is not supported: vm-4 reported MemoryPressure=False with KubeletHasSufficientMemory and 16374180Ki allocatable memory.
Probe-driven termination is not supported: only readiness failures were recorded, while the failed run ended before the liveness probe's 10-second initial delay.
A deployment patch rolled out successfully, and all three required post-recovery windows met the constraints with error_rate=0.0 and p95 latency between 45.34ms and 46.51ms.

closure.summary: The incident is best explained by container-cgroup OOM: the JVM accepted an approximately 512Mi heap ceiling inside a container limited to 256Mi, and Kubernetes recorded OOMKilled/137 restarts while the node had no memory pressure. A deployment patch rolled out successfully, followed by three consecutive healthy SLO windows with zero errors and p95 latency below 47ms. The exact patch contents and direct cgroup memory.events evidence are not present.
